record.title: Beyond Outcomes: Dual-View Relational Learning for Efficient Agent Benchmarking
record.summary: Guo et al. propose DualViewEval, which selects benchmark minisets using both final outcomes and trajectory-process relations. The authors report that, with 20 tasks, the method achieves 24×–40× compression on APEX-Agents and BFCL, reduces MAE by 14.5%–28.2% over the strongest competitors, and improves Kendall tau by up to 7.2% over EssenceBench on SWE-bench Verified. These are paper-reported results across five agent benchmarks, not an independent reproduction or evidence that the selected minisets preserve every capability distinction.

evidence_gaps.description: The paper reports experiments on five public agent benchmarks and comparisons with five compression baselines. the research desk did not rerun the experiments or inspect a released implementation. Cheapest next step: inspect the appendices/artifact and reproduce the 20-task comparison on a held-out benchmark split.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated, trajectory-aware benchmark compression could materially reduce agent-evaluation cost while preserving useful score and ranking information; this is a methods result, not evidence that a small miniset captures all capabilities.
limitations: Results are author-reported in one preprint and were not independently reproduced in this review.
The claims are limited to the paper’s stated benchmark tasks, agents and evaluation protocol; transfer to other workflows or benchmark families is unknown.
Code/artifacts and detailed appendices were not audited in this activation.

technical.demonstrated_result: The accessible preprint specifies the method and reports experiments; the research desk verified the claims in the paper but did not independently reproduce them.
technical.mechanism: The paper proposes and evaluates a benchmark-compression method that jointly uses agent final-score relations and trajectory-process relations to choose an exact-size miniset and predict full-benchmark scores.
technical.regime: Five public agent benchmarks; the quoted compression result uses 20-task minisets on APEX-Agents and BFCL; no independent reproduction.
technical.strongest_baseline: Five representative benchmark-compression methods are compared; the reported gains are against the strongest tested competitor.

brief.title: Beyond Outcomes: Dual-View Relational Learning for Efficient Agent Benchmarking
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported predictive accuracy holds, smaller trajectory-aware minisets could reduce the cost of evaluating agent systems while preserving more ranking and score information than the tested baselines.
